title: Throughput Harmonizer: continuous workload signature profiling and safe coalescence recommendations
creator: Lina Gomez
description:
Goal: Build a continuous 'Throughput Harmonizer' service that derives compact workload signatures from runtime telemetry and emits safe, prioritized coalescence and caching recommendations for Redwood Optimize and the runtime. The Harmonizer should propose grouping/coalescing windows, KV/prefix cache hints, and a conservative 'coalescence budget' that can be safely applied and rolled back with minimal QPS risk.

Background: Current autotune/heuristic systems focus on offline snapshots and per-model heuristics. Teams have asked for lower-latency recommendations that adapt to diurnal shifts and bursty customers without introducing regressions. This ticket implements an online profile extractor + recommendation policy with a built-in canary/rollback mechanism consumable by Console and Optimize.

Design summary:
- Signature extraction: sliding-window summaries per deployment (p95 latency, request size distribution, token length histogram, prefix reuse ratio, KV cache hit estimate, inter-arrival time quantiles). Signatures will be represented as a fixed-length vector (L2-normalized) and a small human-readable label (e.g., "LLM-short-high-reuse").
- Change detection: streaming comparison using an exponential decay distance metric to detect significant workload shifts. Use entropy-normalized cosine distance + significance threshold computed from historical variance.
- Heuristic policy engine: maps signature clusters to recommended parameters: coalescence window (ms), max microbatch tokens, KV prefetch thresholds, cache TTL suggestions, and graceful batching increase steps. Each recommendation has an expected cost delta and estimated latency impact.
- Safe apply primitives: a two-step safe-apply flow (shadow-propose -> canary-apply -> monitor -> gradual-commit). Canary-apply applies the recommendation on a small traffic slice (configurable by route/model), with automated rollback criteria (latency SLO breach, error rate delta, quality regressions detected by the eval webhook).
- Rollback triggers: sharp rise in p95 (>20% over baseline), 5xx rate > 0.1% absolute increase, token cost > 15% above predicted, or eval-set regression > configurable threshold.
- Observability: surface per-recommendation telemetry: expected cost delta, observed cost delta, latency delta, canary duration, rollback reason. Provide a Console dashboard link and a one-click discard/approve.

Integrations:
- Redwood Optimize: export recommendations via recommendations API (POST /v1/recommendations).
- Runtime: apply config through the runtime-config service with versioning and canary flags.
- Console: surface suggestion cards and safe-apply controls.
- Evals: hook to eval service to run small quality checks pre/post apply.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/confluence/throughput-harmonizer (draft)
- Prototype PR (data pipeline): https://github.com/redwood-inference/harmonizer/pull/14
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/r/throughput-harmonizer

Why unique: The Harmonizer focuses on compact, continuously-updated signatures and a formalized coalescence budget that treats batching and cache hints as a single coordinated action — unlike prior tickets that only tuned batching windows or caching independently.

Open questions:
- Appropriate canary traffic percentage for cold-start models vs. steady-state models.
- Frequency of recommendation emission (per-hour vs per-10min) to balance responsiveness and churn.
- Acceptable default rollback thresholds for enterprise SLAs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Service emits signatures for >= 95% of hosted models in staging cluster every 10 minutes.
2) For test workloads, Harmonizer recommendations reduce token cost by >= 8% with <5% p95 latency regression in canary.
3) Safe-apply flow completes canary, commit, and rollback paths automatically per defined triggers.
4) Console surfaces recommendation cards with expected/observed deltas and one-click approve/discard.
5) Unit + integration tests for signature generation, distance metric, and rollback logic present in repo.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy Harmonizer collector to staging runtime for 1 week; collect baseline signatures.
2) Run shadow recommendations in Optimize UI for 3 days and review with SRE/Prod ML.
3) Canary-apply to <1% traffic on low-risk test routes for 48h.
4) If stable, widen to 5% for 72h, then to 20% for 72h.
5) Post-commit monitor for 7 days with automatic rollback enabled.
6) Once stable, enable auto-propose (manual apply) for customer accounts on the Optimize plan.

Has a rollback runbook and alerting playbook (links in design doc).
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Over-aggressive coalescing could increase tail latency. Mitigation: conservative step increases, strict p95 SLO checks, and a KV prefetch safety limit.
Risk: Recommendation churn leading to config thrash. Mitigation: cooldown window (default 6h) per model and signature-change hysteresis.
Risk: Quality regressions from batching/caching. Mitigation: run targeted evals on representative prompt sets before commit; block auto-commit if eval indicates regression.
notes: 2026-02-22: Kickoff sync with SRE, Runtime, and Optimize teams. Agreed to reuse existing telemetry pipeline and add a lightweight signature extractor in the collector. Action: Jordan to prototype extractor in 2w.

2026-03-02: Prototype PR for signature extraction opened (link in description). Initial vector includes token length histogram, inter-arrival quantiles, and prefix reuse ratio. Lina reviewed; requested to add KV hit estimator and to normalize by model sequence length.

2026-03-05: SRE flagged potential cost of extra metrics; we agreed to sample 10% of requests in first pass and then evaluate. Prototype updated to sample and to fall back to snapshot mode when sampling is disabled.

2026-03-09: Design review with PM and Console leads. PM requested explicit expected-cost metric exposed to Console and a manual 'pause' button in the UI. Console will add card placeholder; integration spec due 2026-03-15.

2026-03-12: Implemented change detection threshold tuning in branch. Running e2e experiment in staging cluster now. Observed 12% average cost reduction for targeted workloads with no latency regressions in the 48h run (preliminary). Preparing RFC for security review.
Next steps: finalize canary percent defaults, complete Console card prototype, and open PR for safe-apply orchestrator.
